title: Do the vermin-hunting flags change a WILD animal's behaviour (vanilla gives them only to a pet falcon and a housecat)? CTRL, the tool's HUNT on or off; three of a predatory bird and three of a small land predator placed; every 500 ticks the map's vermin, the vermin within 6 tiles of each subject, each subject's current job, and any report of a catch.
fork: Whether W6 ships as a behaviour or as a label.

predictions.model: the flags act on wild animals
predictions.expects: HUNT-on subjects take vermin jobs or catch reports appear; vermin near them fall

kill_criterion: no vermin job, no catch report and no vermin decline beyond the off arm in both replicate pairs
culling: drop a replicate on any breach or changed save
a replicate whose subjects were not placed is vacuous

arms.name: on
pre: local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local cfg=sw.loadConfig(); if not cfg.initialized then sw.captureDefault(cfg) end; cfg.enabled=true; cfg.groups.enabled=false; cfg.ecology.enabled=false; cfg.hunting.enabled=true; sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.enableSched(); local pool=sw.buildPool(cfg); local bird, small; for _,e in ipairs(pool) do if e.inEmbark and e.layer=='land' then local f=sw.HUNT.wants(e); local st=({sw.RESERVE.of(e.key)})[1]; if f==sw.HUNT.DIVE and not bird and st>0 then bird=e.token elseif f==sw.HUNT.HUNT and not small then small=e.token; if st<3 then sw.RESERVE.set(e.key, 10) end end end end; _G.__x5={bird=bird, small=small}; local _,sp,wr=sw.HUNT.apply(cfg,pool); print(('x5: hunting %s; subjects bird=%s small=%s; %s species, %s caste flags written'):format(tostring(cfg.hunting.enabled),tostring(bird),tostring(small),tostring(sp),tostring(wr)))

local s=_G.__x5 or {}; for _,t in ipairs({s.bird,s.small}) do if t then local ok,out=pcall(dfhack.run_command_silent,'seasonal-wildlife','place',t,'3','land'); print('x5 place: '..(out or ''):gsub('\n',' ')) end end

do: local s=_G.__x5 or {}; local okV,V=pcall(function() return df.vermin.get_vector() end); local nv=okV and #V or -1; local near={}; local jobs={}; for _,u in ipairs(df.global.world.units.active) do local cr=df.creature_raw.find(u.race); local t=cr and cr.creature_id; if (t==s.bird or t==s.small) and not dfhack.units.isDead(u) then local j=u.job.current_job; jobs[#jobs+1]=t..'#'..u.id..':'..(j and df.job_type[j.job_type] or 'none'); local c=0; if okV then pcall(function() for _,v in ipairs(V) do if math.abs(v.pos.x-u.pos.x)<=6 and math.abs(v.pos.y-u.pos.y)<=6 and v.pos.z==u.pos.z then c=c+1 end end end) end; near[#near+1]=c end end; local r=df.global.world.status.reports; local hits=0; for i=math.max(0,#r-60),#r-1 do local tx=r[i].text:lower(); if tx:find('vermin') or tx:find('catch') or tx:find('caught') then hits=hits+1 end end; print(('x5 sample: vermin %d; near subjects %s; jobs %s; report hits %d'):format(nv, table.concat(near,','), table.concat(jobs,' '), hits))

note_rerun: 27 Sep: run 1 was vacuous -- df.global.world.vermin.all does not exist in 53.16 (-1 every sample), and no small land predator on CTRL had stock, so only kestrels were placed. The sample reads df.vermin.get_vector(); the pre stocks the first small land predator to 10 so three can be placed.
